messages:
sanjay: quick dump from today's night profiler + canary logs. short streamed responses (<=16 tokens) show a p95 regression vs baseline. digging in now.

sanjay: short summary: p95 up ~15% for tiny streams at high-concurrency. root candidates: (1) batch formation delay because token_budget waits for more tokens, (2) kernel-selection handoffs triggering workspace & KV pointer rebinds.

sanjay: run snapshot (canary hosts, 48G pool):
```
baseline_p95_no_stream = 40ms
current_stream_p95 = 46-48ms (+15%)
avg_batch_size_stream = 3.1
batch_window_ms = 10-14 (adaptive)
token_budget_target = 64
partial_decode_wait_median = 9.2ms
kernel_select_handoff = 2.6ms
kernel_switches_per_1000 = 42
```

sanjay: KV notes: when partial-decode triggers an early flush and we switch kernel, the KV cache handle sometimes gets rebound which causes extra copies/lookup work. traces show repeated KV pointer refreshes for same session.

olivia: seen similar in session traces—small streams are way more sensitive to micro-ops. proposal: lower token_budget_target for stream routes to 32 and add a tiny fast-path kernel for seq_len<=16 to avoid kernel switch. also try batch_window floor=5ms for streams.

kevin: tiny-kernel sounds good. fairness concerns: if we shorten windows for stream routes we may reduce batching opportunities for longer, bulk routes. recommend per-route throughput_weight and an admission cap. example config: 
```
routes.streaming {
  batch_window_ms: adaptive(5..15)
  token_budget: 32
  throughput_weight: 0.3
  min_window_ms: 5
}
```

mia: ran a short A/B (24h) on dev with window=5ms + token_budget=32 applied only to streaming routes. results: p95_short down ~24%, overall token throughput -4.5%, cost/token neutral. detailed: 
```
p95_short_before = 48ms
p95_short_after = 36ms
overall_tput_before = 1250 tok/s
overall_tput_after = 1194 tok/s
```

mia: partial-decode wait histograms shifted left; KV hit-rate stable but kernel_switch_rate dropped ~60%.

cheng: kernel-selection overhead source: workspace alloc + KV pointer rebind + small runtime init. we can implement a thread-local persistent workspace and a lightweight seq-id handshake to validate KV pointer freshness instead of full rebind. should recover ~1.8-2.4ms per handoff. estimate 3d for prototype.

cheng: caveat: persistent workspace requires careful GC on model reloads and versioned KV pointers. will add seq-id to KV entries to detect staleness cheaply.

kevin: telemetry & SLOs — we need these metrics for automated rollout/rollback: p50_stream_short, p95_stream_short, kernel_switch_rate, kv_pointer_rebind_rate, token_cost_per_1k. set rollback triggers: p95_stream_short worsen >5% OR overall_throughput drop >8% for 15m.

perf-bot: Perf alert: branch "streaming-smallkernel-experiments" @commit 4b9d2f started canary 2026-03-17T15:42:12Z. metric=stream_p95_short increased by 14% on 6% of hosts (investigate).

sanjay: plan: canary 10% traffic with these toggles: token_budget=32 for streaming routes, batch_window floor=5ms adaptive, enable tiny-kernel fast-path for seq<=16 with persistent workspace. telemetry as kevin listed. rollback on the thresholds above.

olivia: I'll own the tiny-kernel PR (workspace reuse + seq-id KV handshake). will include unit + integration tests for model reload scenarios.

kevin: I'll push the per-route queue shaping and the SLO-based rollback logic. also adding guard to avoid floor <4ms to reduce busy spin.

mia: I'll extend the A/B to 48h across a broader set of workloads and collect real-user traces. will capture: partial_decode_wait_p50/p95, kernel_switch_rate, kv_rebind_count, per-route avg_batch_size.

cheng: prototype timeline: 3d for workspace + seq-id, 1d for safety review. after that we can enable in canary.

sanjay: deployment command we'll use (ops-friendly): `/deploy canary streaming-smallkernel --traffic=10% --routes=streaming`

olivia: quick checklist: 
- [ ] tiny-kernel workspace + seq-id
- [ ] per-route adaptive window + token_budget config
- [ ] canary rollout 10%
- [ ] telemetry: p50/p95 short stream, kernel_switch_rate, kv_rebind, token_cost
- [ ] auto-rollback SLOs

kevin: note: also added a CPU guard so adaptive window shrink doesn't spin CPU <4ms. keeping ops cost in mind.
